summary: Server event component added when a passive's boosts were (re)applied. Seen.py context: born in equipment changes, shove/throw, spells, death, dialogues - anything that re-evaluates passives (up to 10 holders at once). Only bg3.exe touches it (no Toolkit reference).

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x32BCAA0 (add helper, called from bg3.exe+0x32B3C00) allocates the 4-byte component and stores 1 as a dword; the caller later stores dword 0 into it on one branch (when the boost list it built is non-empty). macOS default constructor: a single 32-bit store. Live: 2 instances, values 0 and 1. Probably a bool kept in 4 bytes. Second pass: the writer is part of esv::PassiveSystem (bg3.exe+0x32B3C00, called from its per-frame update bg3.exe+0x32B7C70): it builds the passive's boost list (16-byte entries), adds the event with the helper (value 1) and, on the branch where local_518 != 0 and the list is non-empty, overwrites the dword with 0 (line ~651). The whole 4 bytes are one dword store in both places, so the width is established; the meaning of 0 vs 1 is not.

open_questions: Meaning of the value (1 = default from the adder, 0 on one branch of the PassiveSystem writer); bg3.exe+0x32B3C00 has no Toolkit match.
second_pass: Windows adder bg3.exe+0x32BCAA0 (4 bytes, dword 1) and writer bg3.exe+0x32B3C00 in esv::PassiveSystem (dword 0) establish one 32-bit member; its meaning stays unknown, so the name stays field_0.
